o: Recognise brute-force, DoS/DDoS, interception and SQL injection.
Explain the effect of each attack on a system.
Distinguish disruption, theft and unauthorised access.
c: An attacker systematically tries many possible passwords in an attempt to gain access to an account.
A DoS attack overwhelms a service with traffic or requests so legitimate users cannot access it. A DDoS attack originates from multiple systems.
Data may be captured during transmission, potentially exposing confidential information if not protected.
A malicious input may be interpreted as part of a database query, causing unauthorised viewing or alteration of data if the application handles input insecurely.

m.title: Unavailable online resource
m.q: A school's web service receives overwhelming requests and genuine users cannot log in. Explain the likely attack and its effect. [4 marks]
st: The service is overloaded and genuine users cannot access it.
A denial-of-service (DoS) attack targets service availability [1].
Excess traffic or requests [1] overload server resources [1].
Legitimate pupils and staff are prevented from accessing the website [1].

w: An account receives thousands of unsuccessful login attempts. Explain the attack and its likely aim. [4 marks]
A brute-force attack [1] tries many possible passwords [1] seeking the correct combination [1] to gain unauthorised access [1].
A user sends private details on an unprotected connection. Explain data interception and a consequence. [4 marks]
Data interception captures data during transmission [1] without authorisation [1]. Private details may be read [1] and misused for impersonation or theft [1].
An insecure database-backed website misinterprets crafted input as part of a query. Explain the threat and possible damage. [4 marks]
SQL injection occurs when unsafe user input changes a database query [1] so unintended commands are executed [1]. This may reveal private records [1] or alter/delete stored data [1].
wSteps: Focus on repeated guesses, not harmful downloaded software.
The goal is to find valid credentials and enter the account [2].
A brute-force attack [1] tries many possible passwords [1] seeking the correct combination [1] to gain unauthorised access [1].
Describe data in transit and what an eavesdropper might gain.
Someone captures transmitted information without permission [2].
Exposed details may be read and misused [2].
Data interception captures data during transmission [1] without authorisation [1]. Private details may be read [1] and misused for impersonation or theft [1].
Identify the unsafe form or database query.
Stored records may be accessed or changed without permission [2].
SQL injection occurs when unsafe user input changes a database query [1] so unintended commands are executed [1]. This may reveal private records [1] or alter/delete stored data [1].

k.q: Use an already supplied count of failed logins to simulate an account-lock warning. Do not test passwords.
k.code:
failedAttempts = 5
if failedAttempts > 3 then
    print("Account review required")
else
    print("Continue monitoring")
endif
p: Add print("Use secure authentication") at the end.
k.a:
Five failed attempts: Account review required. Two: Continue monitoring.

Extended OCR ERL:
failedAttempts = 2
if failedAttempts > 3 then
    print("Account review required")
else
    print("Continue monitoring")
endif
print("Use secure authentication")

This demonstrates defensive monitoring, not password guessing.

e:
Define a brute-force attack. [2 marks]

Source: Adapted from your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.4.1.
Attempts many possible passwords [1] to discover the correct one/gain access [1].

A museum's online ticket-booking service is deliberately overwhelmed with requests. Explain TWO consequences of the denial-of-service attack for the museum and its visitors. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style question, not a past-paper original.

The booking website becomes overloaded or unavailable [1], so genuine visitors cannot buy or view tickets [1]. The museum may lose bookings/revenue or have increased support work [1], disrupting museum operations [1].

Describe DoS, interception and SQL injection, including an effect of each. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style question, not a past-paper original.

DoS overloads a service [1], causing legitimate access failure [1]. Interception captures data in transit [1], risking disclosure [1]. SQL injection manipulates database queries via unsafe input [1], potentially revealing or changing stored records [1].
v: Denial of Service; overloads availability of a service.
Distributed Denial of Service; traffic from multiple sources.
Capturing information while it is transmitted.
Using unsafe input handling to affect database queries.
x: A DoS attack aims to make a service unavailable to legitimate users.
r: Deceptive messages impersonate a trusted source [1] to trick users into revealing personal data/credentials [1].
State one benefit of agreed networking standards. [1 mark]
They allow equipment/software from different manufacturers to communicate/interoperate [1].
Explain why a computer may run more slowly when it uses virtual memory because RAM is full. [2 marks]
Virtual memory uses secondary storage, which is slower than RAM [1], so moving or accessing data through virtual memory may slow processing [1].
A switch receives data for a printer on its LAN. Explain how MAC addresses support forwarding. [4 marks]
MAC identifies target network interface [1] on LAN [1]. Switch uses MAC destination [1] to forward towards appropriate port/device [1].

priorExam.q: Explain TWO differences between a trojan and a worm, referring to how each gets onto or spreads between computers. [4 marks]
priorExam.a: A trojan is disguised as legitimate software [1] and relies on a user installing or running the disguised program [1]. A worm can replicate itself [1] and spread between computers without a user manually installing each copy [1].
